spokenText:
At the start of the entry record the project name and number, date, full names of the team and general site location. Give a site address, map reference or coordinates as the task provides them. Use enough information to connect the entry to the actual project and place.

Record relevant weather and recent conditions. 'Sunny, eighteen degrees Celsius, light wind' and 'overcast, rain in the morning' are example descriptions. Only write eighteen degrees Celsius as an actual value if it was measured or supplied by an identified reliable source; otherwise describe the weather you can observe and mark the temperature unavailable.

For a simulation, tag the supplied values as scenario data. If the exercise needs a value not supplied, either use an explicitly identified hypothetical addition authorized for that exercise or record 'not supplied'. Do not make an invented weather report look like an observation made outdoors.

Start a new site or day entry when the context changes. Shared day information can be referenced by several samples, but each sample still needs its own collection time, precise location, method and observations.
